summary: IgnisAI is an interactive, Super Intelligence (SI)-powered decision-support dashboard that summarizes, ranks, and interprets 22 NASA microgravity combustion investigations for spacecraft and planetary habitat fire safety (Moon Base >=30% O2 / <=10.2 psi, ISS Cabin, EVA Spacesuit, and Earth 1g baseline). Built on data from NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) repository and NASA's 2015 ISS Combustion Science Researcher's Guide, IgnisAI solves two core challenges: overwhelming experimental data volume and AI hallucination. Every numerical test condition, objective, sensor, and finding in our dataset is verified by an automated script against raw NASA documents (117 verbatim quotes <=20 words). Our two-tier relevance engine separates experiments with verified oxygen and pressure data (Tier 1 Evaluated) from incomplete records and CFD simulations (Tier 2 Unranked), while explicitly flagging the partial-gravity combustion data gap in PSI. An inline-cited RAG Evidence Explorer lets engineers query the NASA corpus with clickable page-level source citations.
details:
### What It Does & How It Works

As human spaceflight transitions from the International Space Station (21% O2, 14.7 psi) to lunar surface habitats and pressurized rovers (expected to operate at >=30% O2 and <=10.2 psi to reduce EVA pre-breathe times), material flammability increases substantially. Researchers and spacecraft engineers navigating NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) database face dozens of heterogeneous microgravity combustion investigations across solid fuels, liquid droplets, gaseous burners, and smoke/dust detectors.

IgnisAI turns these complex records into a transparent, audit-grade engineering triage workflow:

1. Two-Tier Environment Relevance Ranking: Users select a target crew environment (Moon Base, ISS Cabin, EVA Suit, or Earth 1g Reference). IgnisAI calculates a transparent heuristic match score (0–100) weighted across five physical dimensions: O2 Concentration Match (30%), Cabin Pressure Match with explicit atm-to-psi conversion (20%), Fuel Phase Fit (20%), Forced Airflow Regime Fit (15%), and Fire-Safety Function Fit (15%).

- Tier 1 — Evaluated (O2 and Pressure Both Known): Ranks investigations with verified oxygen and pressure data (SoFIE, FLEX, BASS, FLEX-2), displaying a scope chip (Scope: tested, Scope: example, or Scope: planned/capability).

- Tier 2 — Insufficient Condition Data (Not Ranked): Investigations lacking O2 or pressure numbers in our sources (Saffire-I/II/III, BASS-II, ACME CFI-G, CFI, SAME, DAFT, etc.) and CFD simulation studies (PSI-117) are listed below with "—" (no rank number) and explicit missing-field chips so unstated values never artificially outrank measured experiments.

2. 100% Verbatim Quote Verification Pipeline (verify_quotes.py): To guarantee zero fabricated data, every non-null condition (o2_pct_min, o2_pct_max, pressure, flow_speed), objective, variable, key finding, and sensor item across all 22 records must have an exact verbatim substring quote (<=20 words) verified against data/sources/MANIFEST.json (117 verified quotes exported to data/quote_audit.csv). Unknown values are stored as null and rendered honestly as "Not stated in sources".

3. Honest Partial-Gravity Gap Alerts: Because there is currently no partial-gravity combustion data available in PSI, selecting the Moon Base triggers an amber Data Gap Banner explaining that microgravity (0g) and normal-gravity (1g) results can only bound intermediate lunar (~0.16g) and Martian (~0.38g) gravity levels.

4. Cited NASA Evidence Explorer (RAG Chat + Verified Snapshot Fallback): Users can ask free-text questions or click 10 golden queries. The backend retrieves relevant chunks from our 113-chunk page-indexed corpus, enforces an automatic post-check that strips any sentence lacking a valid retrieved [chunk_id], refuses to invent numbers or issue safety certifications, and automatically falls back within 3 seconds to pre-verified snapshot answers if offline.

5. Side-by-Side Comparison & Visualizer: Includes a 2–3 investigation comparison matrix, a qualitative 1g teardrop vs. 0g spherical diffusion flame illustration, a heritage fire timeline (Apollo 1, Apollo 13, Mir, Artemis II), Earth spinoffs, and 1-click CSV/JSON export.

### Benefits, Impact & Creativity

- Accelerates Literature Triage: Helps students, researchers, and fire-safety engineers quickly identify which ISS combustion experiments bound lunar habitat conditions and which records require raw PSI file ingestion.

- Sets a Standard for Scientific AI Honesty: Our creative approach wasn't just to build an AI chatbot, but to build an "Anti-Hallucination" engine. By combining Super Intelligence (SI) with deterministic schema validation and strict substring quote verification, we ensure AI never hallucinates experimental parameters or false safety verdicts.

### Tools, Coding Languages & Software Used

- Frontend: Next.js 14 (App Router), React 18, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Vitest (10 unit tests).

- Backend & Verification: Python 3, FastAPI, Pydantic, jsonschema (Draft 2020-12), Pytest, custom verbatim quote auditor (verify_quotes.py).

- SI / AI Models: Runtime RAG powered by Google Gemini 2.5 Flash with Groq (Llama 3.1) and deterministic snapshot fallbacks. Development-time planning, schema auditing, and code generation assisted by Claude and Gemini.

- Deployment: Static-first frontend on Vercel; containerized non-root Python backend via Docker Compose and Tailscale Funnel.
